gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-osage: Quilon's strokes ebb and flow in weight, editorial and commanding. Noto Sans Osage fills its lines with inflated, rounded bowls and sweeping curves that stay open, giving the heading a friendly counterweight underneath.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Quilon tapers gently wherever its strokes bend and turn, which gives headlines an editorial edge. And Noto Sans Osmanya keeps the paragraphs moving, its s shapes turning wide and easy, its lowercase large beside the capitals.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Quilon moves through moderate shading, round and straight strokes carrying slightly different weights, which gives its display lines an editorial, commanding presence. Noto Sans Palmyrene keeps text moving, its curves stopping short of closing.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Editorial and commanding: Quilon holds the top with gently modulated strokes. But Noto Sans Phoenician does the quiet work, with s curves opening wide at both ends and generous lowercase height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-runic: Quilon lets its stroke weight vary moderately, giving headings an editorial, commanding voice. Noto Sans Runic stays out of the way beneath, with a large x-height, tight ascender room, and curves that never fold back on themselves.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri keeps its ascenders short and its x-height generous, with an a whose lower bowl opens up. Quilon handles the drama; this one handles the paragraphs.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syriac-easter: Commanding from the first glance, Quilon lets mild but visible contrast carry its editorial headings. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern, meanwhile, does the gentler job, with lowercase rising above small caps and curve endings that keep their distance.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syriac-wester: Quilon shifts weight modestly within each stroke, which gives its display lines an editorial, commanding grip. Yet Noto Sans Syriac Western supports it beneath, holding its terminals far from the stroke body, small letters packed like bundled cable.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Quilon keeps a restful line, its stroke weight swinging only modestly, with an editorial, commanding air. And Noto Sans Tai Le joins it with ink strokes that taper out before touching and a minimal step from cap to lowercase.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Noto Sans Tai Viet is a sans-serif with short ascenders, a lofty x-height, and terminals pulled back from where curves close. But if Quilon is made small, its restrained weight gaps fade from view.
